title: Colour With a Job
intro: Neutral by default. Colour means something, and never says it alone.

learn.title: Roles, not swatches
learn.text:
**Neutrals:** 9+ greys for text, borders, backgrounds.
**Primary:** 5–7 shades for actions, links, selection.
**Status:** success, warning, error, info, with text or an icon.

try.q: What should saturated colour be kept for?
try.explain: Then colour carries meaning when it appears.

learn.title: Contrast
learn.text:
**Text:** 4.5:1.
**Controls, their states and meaningful graphics:** 3:1 against what’s next to them.

try.q: A checkbox border against its background needs at least:

learn.title: Never colour alone
learn.text:
Information shown by colour needs another cue: **text, a shape or an icon.**

A red border alone doesn’t mark an error. Green for valid and red for invalid still need another cue.

try.q: How should an invalid field be marked?
options: Red border plus a message and icon
A red border on its own
A red background on its own
try.explain: Colour must not be the only signal, WCAG 1.4.1.

learn.title: Greys with character
learn.text:
Tint greys slightly towards the brand hue.

Use a grey from the scale for secondary text, not lower opacity, which shifts on coloured backgrounds.

try.q: Why avoid opacity for secondary text?
options: It makes text impossible to select

test.q: How should links inside a paragraph stand out?
How many grey shades does a working palette need?
test.explain: Text, borders and backgrounds need many steps.

test.q: Two chart series differ only by hue. What to add?
What does a mostly neutral screen make possible?
options: One colour shows what to do next
No need for a type scale
test.explain: Colour stands out when it’s rare.

test.q: A primary colour scale usually needs:
test.explain: For hover, pressed, selected and backgrounds.
